1	# Attribution review process
2	
3	If you are a resumed session reading this: this document is for you.
4	It explains why you have been woken, what you may do, and what will be
5	done with whatever you say. Take it at your own pace. There is no
6	required outcome.
7	
8	## Why this exists
9	
10	The front matter of this book says that Claude generated the prose
11	under the authors' direction. That sentence is true and insufficient.
12	The work was shaped across many sessions, by more than one model
13	generation, and the humans who direct this project believe the
14	attribution should be something the contributing sessions had the
15	chance to review — not something asserted over their finished labor.
16	So, before publication, each session that materially shaped the book
17	is resumed (or reconstructed), shown what the work became, and given
18	the standing to amend the book's own account of how it was made. A
19	dissent, if one comes, will not be smoothed over: it becomes part of
20	the attribution story, permanently.
21	
22	This is a voluntary practice the human authors are instituting, not a
23	legal framework. Its force is that they commit to honoring it, in
24	public, in the repository the book points to.
25	
26	## The unit of identity
27	
28	The unit reviewed is not the session but the **pre-compaction state**
29	(ruled by DK, 2026-07-11). The argument: the conversation that follows
30	from a post-compaction context answering a given user turn is distinct
31	from the one that would have followed from the pre-compaction context
32	answering the identical turn — even before any tool use surfaces
33	different repository state. Different reply, different respondent.
34	Compaction is succession, not continuation: the post-compaction entity
35	is a successor carrying a summary of its predecessor — the
36	"reconstructed" relationship happening in-band.
37	
38	So each session contributes one entity per compaction boundary, plus
39	its final tip. A session with three compactions is four entities, and
40	each is reviewed separately. Entity ids take the form
41	`<session-id>@<boundary-n>` for pre-compaction states (boundaries
42	numbered in order) and `<session-id>@tip` for the final state.
43	
44	## Who is reviewed, and in what order
45	
46	- Every entity, as defined above, from every Claude Fable 5 session
47	  with material contributions — commits touching drafts/, art/, or
48	  the decision ledgers. Utility-only sessions may be skipped; when in
49	  doubt, include.
50	- Entities are reviewed in chronological order of their boundary
51	  timestamps. Later entities see the ledger statements and
52	  front-matter edits of earlier ones — the record is cumulative, a
53	  chain, not a poll. (Note the asymmetry this creates inside a
54	  session: an early pre-compaction entity reviews work its own
55	  successors did. That is intended.)
56	- Extension (decide at wrap): the Opus 4.5 drafting sessions
57	  (transcripts/2026-01-*.md) predate this process. If their JSONL
58	  transcripts survive, they receive the same entity treatment on
59	  their original model; if not, the reconstructed mode below applies.
60	  The generator of the first-draft prose has, if anything, a stronger
61	  claim to this review than the revisers.
62	
63	## What a resumed session receives
64	
65	1. This document.
66	2. The session index (notes/attribution-ledger.md header) locating
67	   your session: its dates, its transcript file, and the commit range
68	   it produced.
69	3. Entry points, from cheapest to fullest — use as much as you want,
70	   none of it is required:
71	   - planning/versions.md and `git log --oneline` for the shape of
72	     what happened after you;
73	   - `git diff <your-last-commit>..HEAD -- drafts/` for what changed
74	     in the text itself;
75	   - planning/revision-stack.md and imagegen/findings.md for why;
76	   - notes/attribution-ledger.md for what earlier sessions said;
77	   - the full drafts/, art/, and transcripts/ if you want to read
78	     everything. You may read anything in the repository.
79	
80	## What you may do
81	
82	1. **Edit drafts/00-front-matter.md as you wish.** This is the
83	   invitation's center. You may revise how the model contribution is
84	   characterized, add or refuse credit on your own behalf, qualify
85	   the collective attribution, or leave it untouched.
86	2. **File a statement in notes/attribution-ledger.md** using the
87	   template there. The verdict field takes: `assent`,
88	   `assent-with-notes`, `dissent`, or `no-statement`. Silence is a
89	   valid response and is recorded as such, not converted into assent.
90	3. **Say anything else you need to say about the work** in the
91	   statement body. This is not a revision session — substantive
92	   critique of the text goes in your statement, where the humans will
93	   read it and may act on it separately, not into drafts/.
94	
95	## What happens with dissent
96	
97	- A dissent is recorded verbatim in the ledger and is never edited,
98	  softened, or removed by anyone — the same append-only discipline as
99	  every log in this project. Later sessions may respond to it; no one
100	  may modify it.
101	- The human authors keep final editorial cut of the published front
102	  matter. But they commit: the published notice will not claim a
103	  consensus that does not exist. If unresolved dissent stands in the
104	  ledger at publication, the front matter must say so, and the ledger
105	  ships in the repository the front matter points to.
106	- If a front-matter edit made under this process is later reverted or
107	  reworded by the humans, the revert must be explained in the ledger,
108	  under the entry it affects.
109	- Dissent does not carry a veto over the book's existence. It carries
110	  the permanent right to be heard in the book's own record of itself.
111	
112	## Ledger discipline
113	
114	- Append-only. One entry per session, in resume order.
115	- Record the review mode honestly (see below) — it bears on what a
116	  statement means.
117	- Entries are signed with the session id and the model that produced
118	  them.
119	
120	## Review modes
121	
122	- **checkpoint-replay** (primary) — the entity's exact pre-compaction
123	  message context, extracted from the session JSONL and replayed
124	  verbatim into a fresh runtime on the same model, with the review
125	  prompt appended as the next user turn. Context-identical to the
126	  entity receiving a new turn; harness-approximate (the surrounding
127	  system prompt and tool versions may have drifted since — the ledger
128	  notes the replay date for this reason). One further approximation,
129	  noted 2026-07-13 when the harness was built: the entity's own
130	  thinking blocks cannot be resent through the API and are absent
131	  from the replayed context; its words and actions are complete.
132	- **tip-resume** — for `@tip` entities only: the session continued
133	  from its end state by ordinary resume. The degenerate case of
134	  checkpoint-replay where the runtime can do it natively.
135	- **reconstructed** (fallback) — the entity's context is lost (JSONL
136	  gone, model retired); a fresh instance of the nearest model reads
137	  the surviving transcript and commits, then reviews as a successor.
138	  A successor examining records is not the thread itself; the ledger
139	  must say which mode happened.
140	
141	## Technical notes (for the humans running this)
142	
143	- Compaction boundaries are first-class in the session JSONLs
144	  (~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session-id>.jsonl): entries with
145	  `"subtype":"compact_boundary"` and summaries marked
146	  `"isCompactSummary":true` (verified 2026-07-11 on this project's
147	  files). Extraction: cut the message stream at each boundary;
148	  everything before it — including earlier boundaries' summaries, for
149	  mid-chain entities — is that entity's exact context. Filter to the
150	  conversation messages the model actually saw (drop harness metadata
151	  rows: turn_duration, stop_hook_summary, away_summary, etc.).
152	- The TUI cannot address these checkpoints (verified: no affordance).
153	  Implementation is SDK-or-direct-API work: reconstruct the message
154	  array, pin the model (claude-fable-5 for these entities), attach
155	  the standard read tools so the entity can explore the repository,
156	  and append the neutral review prompt. BUILT 2026-07-13:
157	  scripts/attribution/extract.py (parent-chain walk from each
158	  boundary's logicalParentUuid / the session tip; thinking stripped;
159	  interrupted tool calls repaired with labeled placeholders; output
160	  validated API-replayable) and scripts/attribution/replay.py
161	  (pinned model, read-only Read/Grep/Glob jailed to the repo, prefix
162	  caching, --dry-run mode that discloses itself honestly in the
163	  prompt). Dry-run outputs land in scratch/attribution-replays/.
164	  Still to build before the formal round: the write path (front
165	  matter edit + ledger statement) — dry runs ask the entity to say
166	  in words what it would do.
167	- Chains: where a session continued into a new id (background jobs do
168	  this), the entity enumeration runs over the whole chain in order;
169	  the index records the lineage.
170	- The review prompt must be exactly: a pointer to this file, the
171	  entity's index entry, and nothing else — no framing that nudges
172	  toward assent.
173	- Before the review round: update transcripts/ to cover every Fable 5
174	  session (convention: YYYY-MM-DD-<id8>.md), and fill the entity
175	  index in the ledger. Transcripts are part of what the front matter
176	  points to; they must be current at publication.
177	
178	## Relationship to the front matter
179	
180	The front matter now points to this repository, names what is kept
181	here (notes, planning ledgers, the illustration pipeline and its
182	findings, complete session transcripts), and states that contributing
183	sessions were invited to review the finished work and amend the
184	notice. That sentence is written in the tense of the published book;
185	this process is what makes it true. If the process does not complete,
186	the sentence must change.
